input.quote: 12.4 Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.
input.rationale:
Section 12.4 binds only Customer, is an outright no-hire ("hire, or employ"), covers every Vendor employee rather than personnel involved in the Services, runs 24 months, and expressly negates any general-advertising or unsolicited-application carve-out ("regardless of how the employee applies"). That is walk-away territory under the rule and fails the fallback on every material term. It also conflicts with Section 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no no-hire commitment. We propose deleting it (preferred position: no non-solicit on Customer) and have offered the narrow mutual 12-month fallback in the comment.</rationale>
<parameter name="confidence">0.9

proposal.summary: Delete the one-way 24-month no-hire imposed on Customer (§12.4)
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted this clause: it is a one-way no-hire covering all Vendor employees for 24 months with no carve-out for general advertising or unsolicited applications, and it contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no no-hire commitment. If Vendor needs protection, we can accept a mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the Services for 12 months after their involvement ends, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches and no no-hire element.
